source.author: verg
source.text: Ac veluti magno in populo cum saepe coorta est seditio, saevitque animis ignobile volgus, iamque faces et saxa volant furor arma ministrat; tum, pietate gravem ac meritis si forte virum quem conspexere, silent, arrectisque auribus astant; ille regit dictis animos, et pectora mulcet, sic cunctus pelagi cecidit fragor, aequora postquam prospiciens genitor caeloque invectus aperto flectit equos, curruque volans dat lora secundo.
source.text_original: Ac veluti magno in populo cum saepe coorta est / seditio, saevitque animis ignobile volgus, / iamque faces et saxa volant — furor arma ministrat; / tum, pietate gravem ac meritis si forte virum quem / conspexere, silent, arrectisque auribus astant; / ille regit dictis animos, et pectora mulcet, — / sic cunctus pelagi cecidit fragor, aequora postquam / prospiciens genitor caeloque invectus aperto / flectit equos, curruque volans dat lora secundo.
source.text_english: And just as, when a riot has often broken out in a great crowd, and the base rabble is raging in their minds, and already torches and stones are flying, and fury supplies weapons; then, if by chance they have caught sight of some man distinguished by piety and merit, they fall silent and stand there with ears pricked up; he governs their minds with his words and calms their hearts—so all the roar of the sea fell quiet, after the father, looking out over the waters and borne through the open sky, turns his horses and, flying in his chariot, gives the reins a favorable course.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: illis placidi sermonis Iason suggerit affatus turbataque pectora mulcet.
reuse.text_original: illis placidi sermonis Iason / suggerit affatus turbataque pectora mulcet.
reuse.text_english: Jason supplies them with words of calm speech and soothes their troubled hearts.
